recipes.name: Brussels Sprouts Gratin
ingredients_raw: 1 pound Brussels sprouts, cleaned and trimmed
2 slices bacon, cut into 1/2 inch pieces
salt and ground black pepper to taste
2 tablespoons butter, cut into tiny pieces

steps.text: Preheat an oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Lightly grease a baking dish.

Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add the Brussels sprouts and cook uncovered until tender, about 8 minutes. Drain in a colander, then immediately immerse in ice water for several minutes until cold to stop the cooking process. Once the Brussels sprouts are cold, drain well, and cut in halves or quarters, depending on size. Set aside.

Meanwhile, place the bacon in a large, deep skillet, and cook over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until limp and lightly browned, about 5 minutes. Reduce heat and stir in the Brussels sprouts. Season with salt and pepper then toss for about 1 minutes to evenly distribute the seasonings. Arrange bacon and Brussels sprouts on the prepared baking dish. Pour cream evenly over the Brussels sprouts, then sprinkle breadcrumbs and Parmesan cheese on top. Distribute pieces of butter over the bread crumbs.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown and heated through, 20 to 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Brussels Sprouts Gratin
raw_recipe.description: Brussels sprouts are smothered and covered in bacon and cream, then baked to perfection.

video.description: This lovely dish makes an excellent side to fancy up any meal! Flavorful brussels sprouts, mixed with bacon, heavy cream, and topped with bread crumbs is decadent; while the combinations are tremendously delightful. Give it a try!

review.reviewBody: WOW ... 5 stars for a Brussel Sprouts recipe? Great dish. I prepared this for guests last night. I didn't know how they felt about B/S's so I prepared another vegetable side dish as well ... the Sprouts were GONE ..... everyone really complimented the flavor. As is typical I followed the recipe for my first time making it ... no sense in rating a recipe that you've changed!!! The only things I will do differently next time are: 1) skip the butter on top 2) put the bacon pieces on top, not mixed in 3) broil for about 3 minutes at the end. Try this recipe!!!

Loved the flavor! I made a few changes. I used frozen BS that I cut in half and sauted in Butter along with 1/2 a diced onion for about 10 minutes. I only had real bacon crumbles so added 1/2 Cup along with 1 Tbsp of minced garlic & S&P. I didn't have heavy cream so used Half & Half I added the bread crumbs & Parmesan cheese to this and then mixed it all into the BS & bacon. Put into greased baking dish and baked for 20 minutes. Will definitely make again!

This was a super hit with my family and friends! After reading all the reviews, I tripled the bacon and so happy that I did! So one talked about the possibility of preparing ahead of time so, I took a chance and prepared (par boiled) the Brussels Sprouts the evening before. The following afternoon, I browned the bacon, removed to drain on a paper towel and then sautéed the Brussels in some of the remaining bacon fat. I assembled the casserole and let sit on the counter for about an hour and a half before baking and It turned out great!

As a kid I really loathed these misunderstood itty bitty cabbages. But now that I'm a babushka, I appreciate them in ways I never expected. And it's the creativity and palette pleasing innovations of so many cooks here at AllRecipes which are a credit to my turning on this. 

This recipe is very adaptable to modifications according to what you may have on hand. For example, when I made this today, I had no bread crumbs, but I had on hand organic corn chip dippers from Trader Joe's which I placed into a bag and crushed into crumbs. I had no heavy cream, but I had CRÈME FRAÎCHE from Bellwether Farms which I diluted slightly with water - nice upgrade. So yummy and I had some Parmesan cheese choices, but I instead chose Mexican shredded cheese blend which I had on hand.

Trust your 'on hands' items and don't be a scaredy cat to try them. So glad I did that today in Brussels.

I made this for Christmas dinner and it was great. I didn't change any ingredients and it was delicious. You can cook it all with one pan if you use a dutch oven. I boiled the sprouts, not too long! And poured them into a colander to cool then cooked the bacon in the same dutch oven while I sliced the sprouts, then added everything in the Dutch oven when the bacon was done. And threw it in the oven. Will for sure make again.

LOVE this recipe! I first made it as an alternative to green bean casserole a few years ago. Some of my family hadn't tried Brussels sprouts before, and this was a hit. It is a staple at our Thanksgiving table now. I don't boil, cool and then cut the sprouts though. I cut and trim them, microwave for a few minutes, then continue with the recipe. It's true not everyone agrees with microwaving food, but it does save a lot of time especially when cooking for a crowd on a major holiday. Five stars and then some!!!

I made this. Followed the recipe. The only thing I did different, was cooked the bacon and crumbled it up and the tossed the Brussel sprouts and bacon in the reserve. I also added some French’s dried onions with the bread crumbs and parmesan cheese for a little extra flavor. It was a hit on Thanksgiving. I will definitely be making this again.

If you're a brussels sprouts fan, I’d highly recommend that you give this a try, it’s just delicious! I baked for the full 25 minutes, and when I took it out of the oven, the cream was bubbling. Don’t be concerned that it isn’t fully cooked, because the sprouts soak up that cream for a perfectly moist gratin. I used Italian panko breadcrumbs, but I might try some fresh breadcrumbs next time. I mixed most of the bacon with the sprouts mixture, but reserved some for a garnish when it came out of the oven. This one’s a keeper.

This was so good! we were having a meatless meal, so I left the bacon out and sauteed some onions with the Brussels sprouts. I seasoned them with some fresh garlic, salt, pepper and a dash of nutmeg. I used about 3/4 cup cream and sprinkled on the cheese first and then a mixture of Panko and Vigo Italian seasoned breadcrumbs. Everyone loved this. I'll be making this at Thanksgiving for sure!

This was a nice change from plain steamed brussels sprouts. I scaled the recipe down to 2 people, and made it in two individual ramekins. I did follow others' advice, and put the bacon on top, rather than mixing it in.
I had a half orange pepper to use up, so I chopped it and mixed it (not pre-cooked) into the pre-cooked Sprouts, which added nice colour and flavour.
I personally didn't find the heavy cream was a huge bonus in this recipe... will try it next time with buttermilk instead, as that might be just as good.

To save time, I cut them in half first, then boiled for 5 min, tossed into cast iron skillet, fat free 1/2 & 1/2, parmesan, 5 cloves of chopped garlic, garlic POWDER , 2 pinches of salt , 1 pinch red pepper, and bread crumbs. 400 F for 20 min.
Everything is cooked per recipe but it seems saucy. Like too much heavy cream even though I followed the recipe. Hope it tastes good!
My family is crazy about this method of cooking Brussel sprouts!! I will definitely be making this often.
Excellent way to change up and dress up brussels sprouts!

This recipe was very simple to make. When I was blanching the sprouts it crossed my mind that the smell of sprouts was very strong. Once everything was mixed and baking in the oven the smell of parmesan quickly took over. I was pleasantly surprised by my first bite. The cream and parmesan baked into the sprouts making them soft but not mushy. This is a dish I will make again, and I would take to a potluck.

This was a huge hit at my Christmas Day dinner. I made it with vegetarian bacon because 1. I don't like all that bacon grease and 2. That keeps my vegetarian family members happy. You still get the smokey bacon flavor without all the added fat.
Made this for the first time for Christmas dinner, followed recipe exactly, family raved about it (me too!). Delicious!!!

If I was into eating a spoonful of mush with breadcrumbs and cheese on top boy howdy would this be the recipe. Followed all the steps and was rewarded with mushy, overcooked, bland Brussels sprouts. A shame because I love Brussels sprouts and au gratins, but if you like good old roasted Brussels sprouts you might find this recipe lacking.
Yum! I'm doing keto, so I used pork rind "breadcrumbs." Easy and tasty. I think I'll make this for my family at Christmas.
Absolutely delicious! Was a hit and super easy to make.
